transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Evelyn Cho (Redwood SE), Martin Gray (Aurelia Procurement), Leah Ortiz (Aurelia InfoSec), Diego Ramos (Aurelia Cloud), Priya Nair (Aurelia Legal)

Summary:
Quick kickoff between procurement + infosec to validate onboarding gating: MSA/DPA redlines, KMS/BYOK expectations, dedicated trial scope and pricing approval path. Agreed pilot timeline and legal handoff.

Topics Covered:
- MSA/DPA redline process and must-have clauses (data residency, audit rights, liability caps)
- KMS options: BYOK/HSM vs Redwood-managed keys and key rotation
- Deployment mode: Dedicated GPU pool vs Hosted with VPC peering
- Pricing approval pathway and committed spend thresholds
- Audit evidence: SOC2, pen tests, certs

Transcript:
[00:00:09] Samir (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick intro, I'm Samir, AE for Redwood Inference, and Evelyn our SE will run through the KMS options after we align on procurement asks.
[00:00:23] Martin (Procurement): Morning — we have a tight window, procurement board meets next Friday so we wanted to get gating items clarified.
[00:00:31] Leah (InfoSec): Hi — from InfoSec perspective, top of mind: BYOK, audit logs, retention rules, and the ability to rotate keys without service interruption.
[00:00:40] Evelyn (SE): Totally understood. We support Redwood Dedicated with customer-managed keys via our KMS bridge — you can bring keys from AWS KMS or a supported HSM. There's also a Redwood-managed key option if you prefer.
[00:00:51] Diego (Cloud): Sorry to interrupt — can you confirm network architecture? If we do Dedicated, is traffic egress routed through customer VPC, or does Redwood terminate? We need to understand egress and logging.
[00:01:05] Evelyn (SE): For Private/Dedicated we offer VPC peering or PrivateLink. The inference runtime sits on dedicated nodes in our customer segment; egress depends on the peering setup — we can route through your NAT and capture flow logs.
[00:01:18] Martin: Great. On the legal side — Priya will be sending our proposed redlines for MSA and DPA. We need clarity on liability cap, data residency, and whether Redwood will accept certain subcontractor restrictions.
[00:01:31] Priya (Legal): We'll also need an audit clause and the SOC 2 report; plus a clause for incident notification windows that matches our SLA requirements.
[00:01:41] Samir (AE): We can provide SOC 2 Type II and recent pen test summary. Typical incident notification is 48 hours for critical incidents — we can be flexible to 24 hours for escalations in the enterprise tier.
[00:01:55] Leah: 48 is a start, but for certain PII exfil events we need 24 hours. Also require proof of key custody — e.g., attestation that Redwood doesn't have plaintext access to keys for BYOK.
[00:02:07] Evelyn: Under BYOK we never have plaintext key access; keys are in your KMS. For the HSM option we can show the attestation and key wrap logs. Occasionally transcript note: we refer to "K V cache" in the runtime docs, but that's not about keys, sorry — just an audio hiccup.
[00:02:23] Martin: Pricing — procurement needs committed spend options. We prefer a 3 month pilot with a commitment threshold that can accelerate to reserved capacity if accepted. What's your typical pilot to reserved conversion pathway?
[00:02:36] Samir: We do a pilot (2–4 weeks) then a commercial review. For Dedicated, we can offer a time-bound reserved pool with month-to-month onboarding, then convert to a 12-month reserved commit at a reduced unit price. We'll outline tiers: pilot, reserved-3mo, reserved-12mo.
[00:02:52] Diego: Any egress or data-transfer fees we should model? Our infra team flags those as hidden costs.
[00:03:00] Evelyn: We surface egress clearly. For private deployments using your VPC, egress stays in your network (no Redwood egress charge). For hosted API calls across regions there are bandwidth costs — we'll add models in the pricing sheet.
[00:03:15] Priya: On DPA wording — we have a clause that forbids subprocessing without explicit approval. We typically allow a short list of approved subprocessors; can Redwood provide a subprocessors list and commit to notification on changes?
[00:03:28] Samir: Yes, we can provide current subprocessors and 30-day notice on additions. We also have an options doc for on-prem/private installs where we remove subprocessors entirely.
[00:03:40] Martin: For procurement signoff we need two things: 1) commercial terms and workbook for commit tiers; 2) legal redline reconciliation. If you can send both within four business days that would keep us on schedule.
[00:03:53] Samir: We'll get that out — Samir to own the pricing workbook, Evelyn to own the technical runbook and KMS integration examples.
[00:04:02] Leah: One technical question — key rotation. If we rotate keys in AWS KMS, what's downtime? Do we have to warm caches or will requests failover?
[00:04:12] Evelyn: Good question — the runtime supports rolling key rotation. There's a short rekey handshake but no full service outage. You may see a millisecond spike as warmed KV caches are reverified; we log the key rotation event to audit trail. We'll include a sample rotation sequence in the runbook.
[00:04:27] Diego: Also, can we host the model artifacts in our S3 bucket to satisfy data residency and egress? We prefer not to have model weights stored in Redwood-managed storage.
[00:04:38] Evelyn: For Private deployments we support customer-hosted model artifacts mounted via an object store connector. For Hosted you can bring artifacts to a regional bucket and restrict residency; for Dedicated there's an option to host artifacts in your VPC.
[00:04:52] Martin: Regarding SLA — what uptime commitments for Dedicated? And are credits automatic or claim-based?
[00:05:01] Samir: Dedicated has an SLA target of 99.9% for production pools, credits are automatically issued for platform-level incidents and claim-based for tenant-specific issues; we'll walk through the SLA table in the workbook.
[00:05:11] Priya: We also need legal on-boarding path for privileged users — two-person approvals for key rotations, RBAC mapping, SCIM integration for provisioning.
[00:05:21] Evelyn: We support SCIM for user provisioning and granular RBAC; privileged ops can be gated by approval workflows and MFA. We'll include a diagram of the RBAC mappings and an example SCIM payload.
[00:05:33] Speaker 1 (maybe Samir): Quick note on references — procurement always wants 2–3 references in finance verticals. We can provide customers who've run Dedicated workloads in regulated sectors.
[00:05:44] Martin: Yes please, references would help the board. Also provide a short summary of any compliance attestations beyond SOC2 (ISO, FedRAMP posture notes).
[00:05:55] Evelyn: We have ISO27001 in process and a FedRAMP readiness assessment — we'll send a redacted summary.
[00:06:04] Diego: For the pilot, can we get a reserved window where we have guaranteed warm nodes at a smaller scale so our perf tests are representative? We don't want cold-start variance.
[00:06:16] Samir: Absolutely — pilot can include a pre-warmed pool and specific perf SLAs for the test. We'll define token-throughput and p95 latency targets for your workload.
[00:06:27] Priya: A small legal nit — liability cap. Our counsel is pushing for cap at a multiple of fees; Redwood standard is often a fixed cap. Will Redwood entertain a reciprocal cap or specific carveouts for security breaches?
[00:06:40] Samir: We typically offer a fee-based cap and carveouts for gross negligence. We can flag mutual negotiation points, but we'll need your preferred language from Priya so our legal can respond.
[00:06:52] Leah: Also, retention windows for logs and transcripts — we require configurable retention and the ability to purge transcripts on request.
[00:07:02] Evelyn: We support configurable retention per tenant and a deletion API for transcript data. For Dedicated we can set retention to your policy or route logs to your SIEM.
[00:07:13] Martin: Ok, to avoid blockers at the procurement board: please deliver commercial workbook, security pack, subprocessors list, reference customers, and the pilot runbook by 2026-08-18. If legal has redlines sooner we'll try to accelerate the legal-to-legal call.
[00:07:29] Samir: Noted. We'll send an initial bundle by 2026-08-16 and schedule the legal call for 2026-08-19.
[00:07:37] Diego: One more question on escrow — does Redwood have an escrow path for model weights and code in case of acquisition or service discontinuation? Procurement sometimes requires a time-bound escrow.
[00:07:48] Samir: We offer an escrow option for enterprise contracts — typically code and a snapshot of model artifacts can be placed in escrow under negotiated conditions. We'll include escrow terms summary in the workbook.
[00:07:59] Priya: Great. We'll follow up with redlines, and Priya to coordinate internal schedule.
[00:08:06] Samir: Thanks everyone. Quick recap of owners: Samir pricing workbook + references; Evelyn runbook + KMS Terraform examples + security pack link; Priya to send redlines; Martin will collate procurement schedule.
[00:08:21] Martin: Thanks all. Meeting wrap.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Samir to attach pricing workbook and committed-tier examples (CSV + PDF).
- Evelyn to attach a KMS integration example (Terraform snippet), RBAC diagram, and SOC2 report (redacted).
- Legal-to-legal call scheduled tentatively 2026-08-19; confirmation will be sent.

References mentioned: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (placeholder), pricing workbook (link to be attached), pilot runbook (to be attached).

End of transcript.
